A Shiny workflow for diagnosing and modelling **selective disappearance** and **selective appearance** in longitudinal ageing data. It follows the manuscript's Figure 8: look for the signatures in the data (A1–A3), then choose the error family, random effects and ageing function, and compare Models 1–8 (B1–B5).

## Install and run

```r
# from the package root (the folder containing DESCRIPTION)
install.packages(c("shiny", "shinydashboard", "ggplot2", "lme4"))   # required
install.packages(c("glmmTMB", "lmerTest", "DHARMa"))               # count families, p-values, residual checks
source("launch_app.R")                                              # run without installing

# or install the package (DESCRIPTION uses an anonymous placeholder maintainer, which R requires;
# replace it with real details before public release)
install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")   # or devtools::install()
disappR::run_app()
```

## Scripted analyses

The same engine is available from R scripts:

```r
x   <- disappr_prepare(my_data, disappr_mapping(id = "ID", age = "age", trait = "mass", life = "lifespan"))
fit <- disappr_fit(x, models = c("M1", "M2", "M4"), age_function = "Quadratic", family = "gaussian")
disappr_compare(fit); disappr_diagnose(fit); disappr_interpret(fit)
disappr_predict(fit, "M4")
disappr_provenance(fit)
ex <- disappr_example("bouwhuis")            # bundled data, mapping and settings
cat(disappr_code(fit, x, "my_data.csv"))
```
